definition: A paid public garden of the 17th to 19th centuries offering music, lights, food and early rides.
The amusement strip of a fair, named after the Midway Plaisance of the 1893 Chicago exposition.
A picnic and amusement ground built by a streetcar company at the end of its line to sell weekend fares.
An 1880s gravity ride where a car coasted one way, was pushed to a second track, and coasted back.
An early coaster whose cars are guided by side wheels against boards rather than held down on the rail.
A wheel that runs under the rail so a car cannot lift off, patented by John Miller in 1919.
The 1920s boom in wooden coasters that ended with the Great Depression.
Track made from steel tubes that wheels grip on three sides, first used permanently on the Matterhorn in 1959.
A teardrop-shaped vertical loop whose tightening curve keeps forces tolerable, used on Revolution in 1976.
A full-circuit coaster at least 200 ft tall, a class begun by Magnum XL-200 in 1989.
A full-circuit coaster between 300 and 399 ft tall, begun by Millennium Force in 2000.
A full-circuit coaster 400 ft or taller, begun by Top Thrill Dragster in 2003.
A launch that fires a train with a cable pulled by hydraulic motors, as on Kingda Ka.
A launch using linear induction motors along the track, first used on Flight of Fear in 1996.
RMC's steel I-beam track that replaces wooden rails on an existing wooden structure.
A coaster with steel track on a mostly wooden structure, such as New Texas Giant.
The record race for taller and faster coasters that ran roughly from 1989 to 2005.
Disney's trademark for figures that move and speak in sync with recorded audio, first shown in 1963.
Walt Disney's private design company of 1952, renamed Walt Disney Imagineering in 1986.
A designer or engineer at Walt Disney Imagineering; the word blends imagination and engineering.
A continuous chain of swivelling ride vehicles that lets designers point every rider at each scene.
A tracked vehicle with an onboard motion base that adds tilt and bounce, first used on Indiana Jones Adventure.
A dark ride whose vehicles follow a programmed path across a floor using wire or positioning systems, not a track.
The Themed Entertainment Association's peer award for outstanding projects, given since 1994.
A dated booking required to enter a park, adopted widely after the 2020 reopenings.
